item.title: 2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests: At least 140 garment factories close across Gazipur, Savar, and Ashulia, after workers reject the newly announced minimum wage as insufficient, blocking the Dhaka–Mymensingh and Dhaka–Tangail… / Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board raises the monthly minimum wage for garment workers from ৳12,500 to ৳17,000 following a 4–2 vote, a decision rejected by labour unions demanding at least ৳18,000 amid…
item.description:
Image: The Business Standard

At least 140 garment factories close across Gazipur, Savar, and Ashulia, after workers reject the newly announced minimum wage as insufficient, blocking the Dhaka–Mymensingh and Dhaka–Tangail highways and clashing with police firing tear gas and stun grenades.

Sources: The Business Standard, The Daily Star

Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board raises the monthly minimum wage for garment workers from ৳12,500 to ৳17,000 following a 4–2 vote, a decision rejected by labour unions demanding at least ৳18,000 amid nearly a month of labour unrest and hundreds of factory closures.

Sources: AFP, The Daily Star
